key_insight: For strongly adverse-pressure-gradient turbulent boundary layers, the outer layer still shows component-wise similarity when each profile is normalized by a common outer reference location rather than by a new global scaling.
engineering_relevance: This provides a compact way to compare, reconstruct, and model APG boundary-layer profiles for turbulence-model validation, especially in separated or near-separated flows.
method: Assemble a benchmark combining new DNS of a suction–blowing-induced separation bubble with published APG profiles.
Span a wide range of Clauser parameters and Reynolds numbers, then test existing APG normalizations against mean-velocity defects and Reynolds stresses.
Normalize each quantity by its value at a common outer location, using y_s = 0.5δ as the representative case.
evidence_signal: Across β_e≈0.04–180 and Re_θ≈530–19000, the normalized profiles collapse in the outer region, with velocity-defect collapse for y/δ≳0.2 and Reynolds-stress collapse for y/δ≳0.4.
watch_item: The similarity is outer-layer and component-wise only; it does not imply a universal inner-layer collapse or eliminate sensitivity to the chosen reference location within the outer region.
paper_title: Component-wise outer similarity of turbulent boundary layers with strong adverse-pressure gradient
